column3: Close to the Greek.
“Were commended” is rendered “gained approval,” and “the ancients” “the men of old.”
“Ages” is rendered “worlds,” “formed” “prepared,” and “declaration” “word”; NASB follows the critical text (singular “what is seen”).
NASB follows the critical text (“he still speaks”); it supplies “faith” for “it” and adds “though.”
“Translated” is rendered “taken up”; NASB puts the quoted line in capitals.
NASB supplies “Him.”
“Divinely instructed” is rendered “warned by God,” and “moved with fear” “in reverence.”
NASB supplies “when he was” and “by going out.”
“Sojourned” is rendered “lived as an alien,” and “joint-heirs” “fellow heirs.”
“Awaiting” is rendered “looking for.”
NASB does not render “barren,” which is in the critical text, and it omits “gave birth,” a Textus Receptus addition; “power for the conception of seed” is rendered “ability to conceive.”
NASB supplies “as many descendants” and puts the allusions in capitals.
NASB follows the critical text, without “having been persuaded”; “sojourners” is rendered “exiles.”
“Make manifest” is rendered “make it clear”; NASB adds “of their own.”
“Remembering” is rendered “thinking of”; NASB supplies “country.”
“Stretch forward to” is rendered “desire”; NASB supplies “country” and renders “indeed” as “for.”
NASB supplies “son” after “only begotten.”
“Offspring” is rendered “descendants.”
NASB supplies “men”; “in a simile” is rendered “as a type.”
NASB moves “even regarding things to come” to the end.
NASB supplies “leaning.”
“Gave instructions” is rendered “gave orders.”
NASB adds “for.”
Close to the Greek.
“Suffer affliction with” is rendered “endure ill-treatment with,” and “temporary enjoyment” “passing pleasures.”
NASB reorders the clauses; “looking for toward” is rendered “looking to.”
“Anger” is rendered “wrath,” and “persevered” “endured.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB supplies “they were passing through”; “swallowed up” is rendered “drowned.”
NASB adds “after.”
